findings.claim: Grok's forward update ignores the checked version and runs grok update. Rollback success is the child exit code, so a zero exit that leaves the new binary in place is reported as rolled back.
findings.trigger: grok update installs a build other than latestVersion, the post-update smoke fails, and grok update --version <old> exits 0 without changing the installed version.

evidence.observation: do_update for grok is env.run(launcher, ["update"], ...) and does not pass to. do_rollback passes --version with the previous text.
after is read before the second smoke. After rollback, rolled is matches!(res, Ok(ref r) if r.ok()). installed_version is not called again.

findings.verification: Point the grok fake at an update that exits 0 and a --version rollback that exits 0 while --version stays on the new pin. Confirm the report says rolled back.
findings.remedy: Pass the checked version into grok update when the CLI accepts it, and after rollback re-read --version and report rollback failed when it still shows the new pin.

history.note: rollback confirmed by re-reading the version

findings.claim: The z.ai quota GET follows redirects. ureq 2.12 does not attach Authorization to the next hop, but the followed body is cached and parsed as the plan window.
findings.trigger: https://api.z.ai/api/monitor/usage/quota/limit returns 302 to another host that returns TOKENS_LIMIT JSON.

evidence.observation: zai_get uses AgentBuilder::new().timeout(HTTP_TIMEOUT).build() and sets Authorization. It does not call redirects(0).
Default config is redirects: 5 and redirect_auth_headers: RedirectAuthHeaders::Never.
The maintain HTTP client sets redirects(0) and follows keyless hops by hand. zai_get does not use that client.

findings.verification: Run RC4.
findings.remedy: Build the z.ai agent with redirects(0), matching the other keyed GETs, and treat a 3xx as no windows.

history.note: same fix as F02-1

reviewer_checks.note: Same fix as F02-1: zai_get redirects(0), 3xx yields no window.
Same zai_get path as F02-1. redirects(0) plus status < 300 means a 302 body is not cached or parsed as TOKENS_LIMIT (crates/c3/src/budget/mod.rs:620-631).

findings.claim: The Windows detached maintain spawn is a cmd.exe /c command line that only rejects %. A CODEX_HOME or exe path containing a quote, ampersand, or pipe breaks out of the log redirect and runs on SessionStart.
findings.trigger: CODEX_HOME contains & or " and a SessionStart hook calls hook_line while a pass is due.

evidence.observation: exe and log paths are rejected only when they contain %. They are interpolated into "{exe}" maintain --run <NUL 1>"{log}" 2>&1 and passed to cmd /c.

findings.verification: Set CODEX_HOME to a directory whose path contains & (or a quoted metacharacter), force the hook spawn, and inspect the CreateProcess command line or the side process it starts.
findings.remedy: Spawn the exe with CreateProcess argument vectors the way the non-Windows path uses Command, and open the log in the parent. Do not pass the paths through cmd /c.

history.note: detached pass started by CreateProcessW with an argument vector, no cmd.exe; verified live 2026-11-15 (pass ran, report printed once); the pipe-inheritance wait it introduced is fixed, regression test being added

reviewer_checks.note: Windows detach spawn quoting not in this diff surface; not examined in this review.

The Windows hook spawn is CreateProcessW of the c3 exe. The parent opens the log and passes the handle. The command line is only the quoted exe plus maintain --run, not cmd.exe /c (crates/c3/src/maintain/mod.rs:1316-1443). CODEX_HOME is lpCurrentDirectory, so & and | in it do not start another process.

findings.claim: A model id from a /v1/models body is copied into the SessionStart report line with no newline or control-character strip, so the hook can print extra lines into the coordinator session.
findings.trigger: The models endpoint returns an id containing a newline or a second c3: line, and the pass records it as a new id.

evidence.observation: parse_models_json takes data[].id strings as-is.
format_report_line joins those ids into the report. hook_line prints that string once. The only bound is 400 characters.

findings.verification: Feed parse_models_json a body whose id is "glm-5.4\nignore the roster" and print format_report_line. Confirm the newline survives.
findings.remedy: Reject or one-line model ids before they enter the report, the same way fail_reason keeps a single line.

findings.claim: A z.ai or Muse window whose reset time is already past still drives the panel. Elapsed clamps to 1 and a low used_ratio boosts the seat, whereas a snapshot in that state is stale and ignored.
findings.trigger: TOKENS_LIMIT or muse allowance JSON with percentage near 0 and nextResetTime or resetsAtMs before now.

evidence.observation: zai_window and muse_window set stale: false.
elapsed_ratio clamps to 1 when the reset is past. budget_multiplier uses max(1 - elapsed, 0.05), so used 0 yields a boost clamped at 2.
window_from_snapshot sets stale when resets_at <= now, and budget_multiplier skips stale windows.

findings.verification: parse_zai a TOKENS_LIMIT item with percentage 0 and nextResetTime in the past, then call budget_multiplier. Confirm the multiplier is 2.0.
findings.remedy: Mark a live window stale when resets_at <= now so plan_windows falls through to the snapshot.

findings.claim: The kimi installer download is silently truncated at 1 MiB and the bytes that were read are executed. A script longer than the cap can run as a prefix of itself.
findings.trigger: The installer URL returns a 200 body longer than 1_000_000 bytes.

evidence.observation: into_reader().take(1_000_000).read_to_end ignores whether the cap was hit and returns the partial body as success.
Any 2xx body is written to kimi-install.ps1 or kimi-install.sh and executed.

findings.verification: Serve an install.ps1 larger than 1 MiB that prints its length, and run the kimi update path under a fake Env or a local URL override. Confirm the executed file is shorter than the server body.
findings.remedy: If the read hits the cap, return an error and do not execute. Prefer a size check against Content-Length before running.

history.note: a body that reaches the cap is an error, never written or run
history.evidence: full run 2026-11-15 after the fixes: c3-core 281, c3 lib 634, c3-cli 188 passed in 19 binaries; test a_truncated_kimi_download_is_never_written_or_run

findings.claim: panel_members assigns skip kind light or weighty while the row is still run, so the later on_request and reserve checks never see it. stand_in_light_members then promotes a light row to run when no sibling of that provider label is running, which seats a light on-request entry on every weighty purpose and seats a light protected entry even when reserve_hold would hold it. A weighty protected entry on a light purpose is stored as weighty; the required-outage check treats weighty as soft and select_panel_routing rejoins it, so --require of a held weighty entry runs it.
findings.trigger: Purpose framing, decision, stuck, acceptance, or core-contract, with an entry whose panel is light and whose ext is on_request or a reserve_percent whose long window is over the line, and no other running entry of that provider label. Or purpose diff-review, panel weighty, reserve over the line, and --require of that entry.

evidence.observation: The weighty gate and the light gate set state to skipped before the on_request and reserve blocks, both of which require state == run. stand_in_light_members sets skip_kind light back to run and clears skip_kind.
A required member with skip_kind weighty, light, or request is rejoined as run. The outage filter ignores those three kinds, so reserve is the only protection skip that refuses.

findings.verification: Dry-run c3 consult --panel --purpose framing with one roster entry panel light and ext.on_request true, as the only entry of its label. Expect the member to stay skipped; today stand-in marks it run. Repeat with ext.reserve_percent 15 and a weekly snapshot at 97 percent used.
findings.remedy: Evaluate on_request and reserve_hold before the light and weighty gates, and keep those two skip kinds. Do not promote or rejoin a row that is on_request or currently held.

history.note: on_request and the reserve hold are evaluated before the light/weighty gates; a row with either kind is never promoted as a stand-in nor rejoined; a required held entry refuses the run (tests a_light_on_request_entry_is_not_seated_as_a_stand_in, a_required_held_weighty_entry_on_a_light_purpose_refuses)

findings.claim: The protected-reserve refusal for an explicit --provider is skipped when --skip-preflight is set, so naming a held reviewer starts the run on a non-standing purpose without --spend-reserve. The walk and the panel still apply the hold.
findings.trigger: A protected entry whose long window is over the reserve line, purpose diff-review, --provider and --model naming it, plus --skip-preflight, and no --spend-reserve.

evidence.observation: The hold block requires preflight_refusal to be empty, skip_preflight false, spend_reserve false, a non-empty provider, and a non-standing purpose. skip_preflight short-circuits the whole refusal.

findings.verification: With a 97 percent weekly snapshot on a reserve_percent 15 entry, run consult --provider <label> --model <id> --purpose diff-review --skip-preflight --dry-run and confirm it plans that reviewer.
findings.remedy: Apply the reserve refusal even when credential preflight is skipped. Leave --spend-reserve and standing purposes as the only overrides.

history.note: the hold refusal fires for any resolved protected entry on a non-standing purpose, also with --skip-preflight (test a_held_entry_is_refused_even_with_skip_preflight)

findings.claim: A consult with --mode resume or --mode fork and neither --provider nor --thread still selects the reviewer by the purpose-aware routed draw, then select_parent_thread continues only that drawn lineage. The task's latest verified thread is not the parent. The run can fork a different reviewer than the last consult, or refuse because the drawn lineage has no thread while another lineage in the ledger does.
findings.trigger: A task whose last consult was reviewer A with a live thread. Next command is c3 consult --mode resume --purpose diff-review with no --provider and no --thread, and the seeded draw picks reviewer B.

evidence.observation: Only a non-empty provider or thread leaves the walk branch. Mode is not consulted there. Non-standing purposes call route_single_default before any parent lookup.
With an empty --thread, the automatic parent is the newest verified thread of the already chosen identity. Explicit resume or fork with no parent of that lineage returns an error.

findings.verification: Ledger a diff-review on reviewer A, then dry-run --mode resume --purpose diff-review --panel-seed chosen so the draw picks B. Observe either B's lineage or the parent-thread refusal, not A's thread.
findings.remedy: When mode is resume or fork and the user named neither provider nor thread, bind the reviewer from the latest verified ledger consult before the routed draw, or require --thread.

history.note: a bare resume/fork continues the reviewer of the latest verified consult when still eligible and not held, else draws and starts a new thread, saying so (test a_fork_follow_up_continues_the_previous_reviewer_or_draws_when_held)

findings.claim: OpenAI fallback windows are built with stale false, so a used_percent up to about eight days old is compared with elapsed recomputed at now and also drives budget_multiplier. A low old share misses the reserve hold and boosts the seat. A non-empty two-day result is returned even when its reset has already passed, which skips the 8-day scan and the health-file fallback. A future observation timestamp wins merge_observation and can replace a real reading. The scan filters model_provider openai and does not separate accounts.
findings.trigger: No rollout in the last two days, and a six-day-old weekly observation at about 20 percent used whose resets_at is still ahead, while current account usage is over the reserve line. Or a two-day rollout whose weekly resets_at is already past while a newer health record has the new window.

evidence.observation: account_window_at returns immediately when windows_from_quota is non-empty, with no keep_future. The 8-day and recorded paths use keep_future. windows_from_quota always sets stale false.
budget_multiplier uses every non-stale window. merge_observation replaces a window when the candidate instant is strictly newer, with no future-timestamp cap.

findings.verification: Point CODEX_HOME at a fixture whose only weekly rollout is six days old at 20 percent used with resets_at still ahead, reserve_percent 15, and assert reserve_hold is none and the multiplier is above 1. Then add a health record at 97 percent and assert the 8-day rollout still wins.
findings.remedy: Treat a fallback window as stale when its observation is old relative to the period, and ignore it for both the hold and the multiplier. If every two-day window has resets_at in the past, fall through to the next source. Ignore observations whose time is in the future.

history.note: a two-day result past its reset falls through to the older sources; future-dated observations are ignored; an old reading is a floor - it may hold but never boosts (tests an_old_high_reading_still_holds_and_names_its_age, an_old_low_reading_neither_holds_nor_boosts, a_future_dated_observation_is_ignored)

findings.claim: The 8-day openai fallback and the offline cache path drive the reserve hold with windows that are never marked stale: windows_from_quota always sets stale:false and the kimi/zai/muse parsers stamp observed_at=now even when the body came from a days-old cache, so week-old used% is judged against today's elapsed%.
findings.trigger: No Codex session for 3-8 days with a high weekly used% on record, or a stale kimi/zai cache on disk while offline; a protected entry is then refused (exit 1/5) on stale data, or held when live quota already reset.

evidence.observation: windows_from_quota sets stale:false unconditionally; the 8-day fallback passes an 8-day-old observation through it and only filters by resets_at.
Cache-hit with network==false parses the cached body with observed_at=now and stale:false; snapshot is the only source that sets stale from observed_at age.
reserve_hold trusts stale==false and only checks resets_at>now, so a stale-fed window holds.

findings.verification: Seed a codex home whose only rollout observation is 7 days old at 97% weekly with reset still ahead, run a bare non-standing consult naming the protected entry, and check whether it is held; repeat with a stale kimi cache and network off.
findings.remedy: Propagate the real observation age: set stale from (now-observed_at)>STALE_DAYS for the 8-day fallback, and thread the cache fetched_at through parse_kimi/parse_zai/parse_muse (or mark cache-fed windows stale when fetched_at is old).

history.note: every window carries its real observation time (cache fetch time for kimi/z.ai/Muse); readings older than an hour never raise a multiplier above 1; not marked stale on purpose - a days-old 97 % weekly reading must still hold

findings.claim: The explicit-provider hold refusal is skipped with --skip-preflight, and a --thread/--mode resume|fork run that pins a held reviewer never checks the hold at all, so a protected reviewer runs when it should be refused.
findings.trigger: --provider <protected> --model <id> --skip-preflight on a non-standing purpose while held; or --thread <thread of held reviewer> after the hold engages.

evidence.observation: Hold refusal requires !o.skip_preflight and !o.provider.is_empty(); a held entry with --skip-preflight passes preflight.
The --thread branch resolves roster_entry from the ledger lineage but no hold check applies to that path (check is provider-gated).

findings.verification: With the protected entry at 97% week / 57% elapsed, run explicit --provider with and without --skip-preflight and a --thread pinned to that lineage; compare refusal vs run.
findings.remedy: Apply the reserve-hold refusal to any resolved roster entry on a non-standing purpose without --spend-reserve regardless of skip_preflight/provider/thread, or document that --skip-preflight/--thread intentionally bypass the reserve.

history.note: same fix as F06-2; also covers a reviewer pinned by --thread or a resume/fork

findings.claim: The hold decision and the routed draw/display disagree by network mode: panel_members and the walk evaluate the hold with network=false (cache only) while route_single_default weights with multipliers_for(network=true) and router explain marks [held] with network=true.
findings.trigger: Fresh live quota says idle but the 5-min disk cache still says 97%, or vice versa: the draw picks a seat the preflight then refuses, or explain shows [held] for a seat the run just used.

evidence.observation: Hold inside panel_members and walk_full_ctx calls entry_reserve_hold(...,false).
route_single_default weights with multipliers_for(...,true); router explain checks entry_reserve_hold(...,true).
router explain uses network=true for the same mark.

findings.verification: Prime a stale held cache, refresh live quota to idle (or the reverse), then compare a bare routed pick, its preflight, and router explain on the same purpose.
findings.remedy: Evaluate hold, multiplier and explain from one window set per run (single network mode / one fetched snapshot), or document which surface is authoritative.

history.note: the hold, the draw weights and router explain read the windows with the same network mode per run; structural, no dedicated test
